title: Indian-Origin Engineer Uday Ruddarraju Elevated to CTO of Compute at OpenAI
excerpt: Ruddarraju, who built xAI's Colossus supercomputer with 250,000 GPUs, was promoted from Head of Compute Infrastructure after joining OpenAI a year ago.
body:
• Uday Ruddarraju has been promoted to Chief Technology Officer of Compute at OpenAI, rising from Head of Compute and Infrastructure.
  • He joined OpenAI in July 2025 after leaving xAI, where he built Colossus — a supercomputer housing over 250,000 GPUs — and led the training of Grok 3.
  • The promotion signals OpenAI's deepening investment in compute infrastructure as it scales the Stargate initiative.
  • Ruddarraju holds a master's in computer science from the University of Minnesota and previously held senior roles at Robinhood and eBay.

From Colossus Builder to OpenAI's Compute Chief

OpenAI has elevated Uday Ruddarraju to the role of Chief Technology Officer of Compute, according to a report by Exchange4media on July 18. Ruddarraju had been serving as Head of Compute and Infrastructure since joining the company in July 2025, and his promotion places him at the helm of one of the most critical functions in the AI industry — the infrastructure that powers frontier models.

The appointment comes at a pivotal moment for OpenAI. The company is scaling its Stargate infrastructure initiative, a next-generation compute platform designed to support future iterations of its most advanced AI models. Ruddarraju described the project as "a high-stakes infrastructure challenge that aligns well with the kind of ambitious work" he is passionate about, speaking to Wired when he first joined.

The Colossus Chapter

Before OpenAI, Ruddarraju spent just over a year at xAI, Elon Musk's artificial intelligence startup, where he served as Head of Infrastructure Engineering. His most consequential achievement there was leading the construction of Colossus, a supercomputer housing more than 250,000 GPUs — one of the largest AI compute systems ever built. He also oversaw the training of Grok 3, xAI's flagship model, running the largest known pre-training operation across 100,000 GPUs at the time.

"His most consequential achievement there was leading the construction of Colossus, a supercomputer housing more than 250,000 GPUs — one of the largest AI compute systems ever built."

"His most consequential achievement there was leading the construction of Colossus, a supercomputer housing more than 250,000 GPUs — one of the largest AI compute systems ever built."

"When I first joined, I thought everyone was absolutely nuts for thinking we could deploy 100K GPUs in 4 months, especially without a fully functioning site. Watching us go and double that and most importantly successfully train Grok 3 made me incredibly proud."

— Uday Ruddarraju, on his time at xAI

In his farewell message on X, Ruddarraju praised Musk's teams and referenced Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's assessment of xAI's capabilities: "Jensen Huang was right — Elon and his teams are singular in what they can achieve."

The Career Path

Ruddarraju's journey to the top of AI infrastructure traces through some of America's most prominent tech companies. He earned a bachelor's degree in computer science from Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology in Hyderabad before completing a master's at the University of Minnesota.

He spent five years at eBay from 2013 to 2018, where he worked on Kubernetes adoption and cloud infrastructure. He then joined Robinhood, the financial services platform, spending nearly seven years and rising to Senior Director of Engineering and Head of Infrastructure. During his tenure, Robinhood scaled from one million to 24 million users, and Ruddarraju led a team of 160 engineers.

A Pattern of Indian-Origin Leadership in AI

Ruddarraju's elevation continues a broader trend of Indian-origin engineers rising to senior leadership positions at the world's most influential AI companies. His promotion comes alongside other recent appointments: Google DeepMind, Microsoft AI, and Meta's AI research divisions all have Indian-origin leaders in key technical roles.

At OpenAI, Ruddarraju was one of four notable hires when he joined in 2025, alongside David Lau from Tesla, Mike Dalton from xAI and Robinhood, and Angela Fan from Meta. Greg Brockman, OpenAI's co-founder and president, personally welcomed the group in a public announcement on X.

What's Next

As CTO of Compute, Ruddarraju will oversee the infrastructure backbone that underpins OpenAI's model training and deployment. With Stargate positioned as a central piece of the company's strategy, his track record of building massive compute systems — from Colossus to Robinhood's rapid scaling — makes him a natural fit for the challenge ahead. The role puts him at the intersection of hardware engineering and AI research, a domain where execution speed increasingly determines competitive advantage.
